title: Failure Replay & Trace — UX notes and wireframes
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a proposal for a "failure replay" and request-trace UX inside the Redwood Console. Goal: let engineers and SREs rapidly investigate intermittent failures (timeouts, 5xx, model runtime errors) by replaying a single failed request end-to-end, inspecting routing choices, model variant fallbacks, and token-level model outputs.

Context / why this exists:
- We get frequent support tickets and SLO alerts where root cause is unclear: client timeout vs. model crash vs. infra preemption.
- Existing error dashboards show aggregates and examples but not an actionable single-request replay that reproduces path-dependent failures (e.g., KV cache miss + batch placement).
- A focused replay view reduces time-to-resolution and provides evidence for support and product teams (repro payload, kernels chosen, env).

Primary users / personas:
- Platform/SREs: triage incidents across Dedicated fleets and Hosted API customers.
- ML engineers: debug model mismatch/regression where output suddenly changes or throws model errors.
- Solutions engineers / support: reproduce customer-reported failures and generate recommended mitigations.

Key user stories:
1) As an SRE, I want to select a failed request and replay it at the same routing decisions (region, model variant, quantization) so I can confirm whether the failure is deterministic.
2) As an ML engineer, I want to compare the failed request's token-level logits/decoded outputs across two model variants to see where divergence happens.
3) As a support engineer, I want a minimal export (request payload, model version, runtime logs) to attach to a bug/PR.
4) As a product engineer, I want to see whether a fallback policy (e.g., route to cheaper model) executed and whether that contributed to increased 5xxs.

High-level interaction flow:
- List view: filterable table of failed requests (filters: time window, failure type (timeout/5xx/model_error), model family, region, customer id). Click a row -> opens Replay Workspace.
- Replay Workspace (three-column layout):
  1) Left: Request metadata + timeline (ingest -> routing -> runtime -> response/error). Timeline shows duration, queueing, batch placement, cache hit/miss. Click any segment to show logs.
  2) Center: Live replay player. Buttons: Replay at-time, Replay with current infra, Replay with alternate model variant, Re-run with tracing enabled (heatmap of token latency). Player shows streaming tokens if successful, or synchronous error details.
  3) Right: Artifact panel. Tabs: Runtime logs (truncated), Model outputs (tokens + scores), Kernel & hardware selection, Fallback trace, Export.

Wireframe notes (visual language):
- Timeline should be a stacked horizontal bar (ingest/route/queue/execution/encode) with mouseover tooltip showing ms and link to logs. Colors indicate anomaly buckets (red = error, orange = high latency).
- Replay player uses streaming prefix so users see early divergence. Include a "diff mode" toggle: overlay outputs from two replays (original failed attempt vs. replay) with alignment markers and first-divergence highlight.
- Logs are collapsed by default with ability to expand to full trace. Limit large logs to 5k chars in UI and provide export link.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Can select a failed request and run a deterministic replay against the same model variant and runtime config.
- Timeline shows at least: total latency, routing decision, cache hit/miss, batch id (if present), infra node id.
- Replay shows streamed tokens when available and provides the raw exception/log when failing.
- Export bundle includes request JSON, routing metadata, runtime logs, model version hash.

Non-goals (MVP exclusions):
- Full fidelity cross-environment reproducibility (we will not spin up customer private infra in MVP).
- Automatic root-cause attribution (we will surface signals, not assert cause).

Backlog & grooming notes (rough prioritization):
- (P0) Replay runner + timeline + export bundle — RINF-4021
- (P1) Diff mode for token streams + side-by-side variant compare — RINF-4024
- (P1) Filters for failure reason and customer id on list view — RINF-4030
- (P2) Tracing-enabled replay that records per-token kernel selection — RINF-4041
- (P2) Playbook suggestions (automatic mitigation hints) — RINF-4050

Edge cases & privacy considerations:
- Customer data in request payloads: export must respect workspace/data retention/export policies. Add a consent checkbox for exporting for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private, follow local retention.
- Replaying requests that mutate state: disallow or sandbox replays; MVP will only replay idempotent generation calls.

Open questions for engineering / SRE:
- How deterministic is replay across model variants when non-deterministic kernels are used? (Samir to confirm)
- Can we guarantee same batch placement for replayed request or do we simulate a single-request batch? (Luis to prototype)
- Cost/ops implications of allowing arbitrary replays on Dedicated infra (throttling)?

Proposed copy (UI microcopy):
- Replay button: "Replay request — preserve original routing"
- Alternate replay: "Replay with current infra (non-deterministic routing)"
- Timeline tooltip example: "Queue: 12 ms — placement wait (batch id: 1221)"

Mockup checklist for design handoff:
- Artboard: List view + Replay Workspace (desktop 1440).
- Components: timeline component, streaming player, token diff component, logs accordion, export modal.
- Interaction spec: hover, click-to-expand, keyboard shortcuts (r = replay, e = export).

Next steps / owners:
- Prototype: front-end wireframes + basic player with canned replay data (Priya) — due 2025-01-24.
- Backend replay runner spec (Samir + Luis) — draft 2025-01-22.
- Security review for export flow (Alex) — check-in 2025-01-27.

Notes from meeting 2025-01-15:
- Decision: MVP will avoid running stateful customer requests; only allow generative endpoints.
- Action: add a throttling gate controlled by product flags for Dedicated customers.

Appendix: quick mock scenarios
- Scenario A (timeout): Request A shows 2s queue + 3s execution + client timeout at 6s. Replay confirms execution succeeds under lighter load -> root cause likely queuing.
- Scenario B (model error): Request B raised "CUDA OOM" in runtime logs. Replay against a quantized variant succeeds -> indicates memory footprint regression.
- Scenario C (fallback cascade): Initial model responded with 5xx, fallback to cheaper model returned hit but with degraded quality; diff mode will show token divergence and help decide whether to disable fallback policy.

If you have more edge cases or wants a different layout (e.g., single-column mobile-first), drop comments below.
